title: What's new in BrickVerse Creator
subtitle: Preview experiences across devices, experiment with VR, and keep published project details in sync.

sections.title: New beta: Device Emulator
sections.body: Test responsive experiences and input behavior across more target devices without constantly changing hardware.
items: Preview phone, tablet, console, desktop, and VR device profiles from Tools > Device Emulator
Display phone, tablet, TV, and landscape screen-size guides directly over the editor viewport without starting a play test
Inject fake thumbstick, gamepad button, trigger, touchscreen, headset, and VR controller input into the active play-test client
Emulated Input.DeviceType, LastInputDevice, touchscreen, gamepad, and VR state use the same runtime paths as real devices
Device Emulator is opt-in from Beta Features and can be enabled or disabled without restarting Creator

sections.title: Experimental VR and gamepad support
sections.body: BrickVerse experiences can begin targeting connected PC headsets and standalone XR builds while the APIs continue to evolve.
items: Experimental OpenXR runtime support for PC-connected headsets and XR-enabled exports
New Luau VRService access to headset and hand poses, tracking state, controller modes, navigation, recentering, and haptics
Headset and controller movement can drive character VR poses and common gameplay actions
Gamepad navigation and device reporting support console-style play and Creator input simulation
OpenXR stays disabled in normal non-XR exports, preventing unsupported-headset startup alerts

sections.title: New beta: Animation Editor
sections.body: The experimental Animation Editor is available for creators who want to test the unfinished animation workflow and share feedback.
items: Animation Editor now has its own explicit Beta Features enrollment
The Tools menu remains locked until the beta is enabled
Beta enrollment updates menu availability immediately without requiring a restart
Clear instability and compatibility messaging sets expectations while the workflow is under development

sections.title: Device-aware runtime debugging
sections.body: Creator and play-test clients now exchange richer device state through the existing runtime debugger connection.
items: New debugger messages carry device profiles, controller axes and buttons, VR poses, and tracking state
Emulation settings automatically reapply when a new play-test client connects
Fake VR input is exposed to Luau through VRService signals and user CFrame APIs
Synthetic gamepad events pass through Godot's normal input pipeline so game code can be tested realistically
The emulator reports whether input is live or requires an active play test

sections.title: Recent projects stay current
sections.body: Creator's home screen now follows the latest published universe metadata instead of relying on stale local placeholders.
items: Recent-world cards load the current primary thumbnail URL from the BrickVerse API
Opening or refreshing a project updates its universe name, primary world ID, thumbnail ID, and cached thumbnail URL
Modern 64-bit thumbnail IDs are supported without overflowing older metadata fields
Metadata refresh waits for Creator authentication and uses the authenticated OAuth API client
Offline projects continue using their last cached metadata instead of failing to open

sections.title: A clearer Creator interface
sections.body: Common actions are easier to recognize, and experimental tooling is clearly separated from stable workflows.
items: File, Edit, Insert, Model, Tools, View, Help, and Dev actions now use consistent SVG icons
Input Manager is available from Tools with a dedicated keyboard icon
Device Emulator and Animation Editor show contextual beta-lock tooltips when unavailable
Beta feature changes propagate live to their menu entries
What's New continues to work offline using this packaged release feed
